metadata.title: Will Shipley leads underwhelming backfield attack in Week 12 win
metadata.description: Will Shipley rushed 10 times for 46 yards while also failing to catch his only target in the Eagles' 39-38 Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Shipley has struggled to find running room out of the backfield, rushing for under 50 yards in each of his seven games. The running back could be in line for increased snaps with Saquon Barkley (stinger) exiting early Thursday, but remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 13 contest against the Arizona Cardinals.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Leads backfield in Thanksgiving win
metadata.description: Shipley carried the ball 10 times for 46 yards and failed to catch his only target in Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Saquon Barkley (neck) exited the game early with a stinger, leaving the backfield in the hands of Shipley. The Eagles had to abandon the run game after halftime, however, limiting his usage as Joe Milton engineered an incredible comeback with his arm and legs. Barkley spent most of his time on the sideline trying to talk the coaching and training staffs into letting him back on the field, suggesting his absence was just precautionary, but if he misses additional action, Shipley could be in line for a much bigger workload in Week 13 against the Cardinals.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) off injury report for Thursday
metadata.description: Will Shipley is off the injury report for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Shipley was limited in practice on Wednesday. He'll remain in his backup role behind Saquon Barkley.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Ready to go for Thanksgiving Day game
metadata.description: Shipley (illness/foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Despite being listed as a limited participant throughout the week, Shipley made enough improvement in his recovery from an illness and his lingering plantar fascia injury to get the green light to play Thanksgiving Day. Shipley is expected to contribute as a kickoff returner along with serving as the top backup out of the backfield to Saquon Barkley. In his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve during last week's win over the Steelers, Shipley carried four times for nine yards while playing 19 of 53 snaps on offense.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) limited in practice Tuesday
metadata.description: Will Shipley was limited in practice on Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Shipley remains a pure stash when he is healthy.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Remains limited Tuesday
metadata.description: Shipley (foot/illness) was a limited participant at the Eagles' walkthrough practice Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Shipley remained limited for a second day in a row while dealing with an illness and a foot injury. The running back returned to action in Week 11 after missing four games with a foot injury, and the illness is likely the more substantial concern at the moment. Shipley will have one more chance to be a full participant at Wednesday's final session ahead of Thursday's matchup with the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Under the weather
metadata.description: Shipley (foot/illness) was estimated as a limited participant on Monday's injury report.
metadata.analysis: Shipley returned Sunday from a four-game absence due to a foot injury, and he finished that contest with four carries for nine yards and returned three kickoffs for 75 yards. He's still working through that foot issue, but he's now battling through an illness, so his practice participation over the next two days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day contest against the Cowboys in Dallas. Shipley could operate in an elevated role on offense Thursday depending on the status of Saquon Barkley (neck/illness).

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) limited in estimated practice Monday
metadata.description: Will Shipley was listed as a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
metadata.analysis: Shipley saw four carries in his return to action on Sunday. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Will Shipley has minimal production in return to action
metadata.description: Will Shipley rushed four times for nine yards in Sunday's win against the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Shipley returned from a stint on IR and saw limited work upon his return. However, if Saquon Barkley (arm) is unable to play on Thursday, Shipley will fall into late RB2-mid- RB3 value against the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Offers Insurance Amid Teammate's Injury Uncertainty
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley could become a worthwhile waiver-wire pickup following Saquon Barkley's (arm) injury in Sunday's 19-16 win over Pittsburgh. Barkley exited in the fourth quarter with an apparent left arm/shoulder injury and did not return. Shipley, activated from injured reserve ahead of the game after recovering from a foot injury, stepped into the backfield after Barkley left. He finished with four carries for nine yards. Barkley expressed optimism about playing Thursday against Dallas, although his availability remains worth monitoring on a short week. Shipley has limited standalone fantasy value but could be a useful injury replacement if Barkley can't play. Managers rostering Barkley may want to secure Shipley as insurance ahead of Thursday's game.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Cleared to return for Week 11
metadata.description: Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
metadata.analysis: Shipley was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the third-year running back has been officially cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a partial plantar fascia tear that he sustained in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley and Jaydon Blue will operate as the Eagles' rotational running backs behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against a Steelers defense that ranks third in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (83.2).

metadata.title: Will Shipley Active Against Steelers
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley (foot) is officially active for the Week 11 game on Sunday against the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers, according to the team. Shipley is back for the Eagles after being officially activated from Injured Reserve on Saturday. The 24-year-old should operate as the primary backup to starter Saquon Barkley, who has battled through back and hamstring injuries in recent weeks. The former fourth-rounder in 2024 from Clemson should only be considered a handcuff option in deeper fantasy football leagues as long as Barkley is healthy and active for the Eagles. Shipley had a limited role in the first five games of the 2026 season before landing on IR, carrying the football 20 times for 57 yards (2.9 yards per attempt) and one touchdown on the ground while adding only five receptions for 31 yards on eight targets as a receiver out of the backfield. In his first game back this weekend in Philly, Shipley probably will not have a huge role as a change-of-pace option behind Barkley unless Barkley has a setback with his hamstring or back against Pittsburgh.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Activated from IR
metadata.description: The Eagles activated Shipley (foot) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Shipley logged an LP/LP/DNP practice regimen during Week 11 prep, with Friday's absence attributed to an illness. He appears to be closing in on his first game action since Week 5, when he suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia, but his status for Sunday's matchup won't be confirmed until about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Assuming Shipley returns to action this weekend, he may serve as the direct backup to top RB Saquon Barkley.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot) activated from IR
metadata.description: The Eagles activated RB Will Shipley from injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: Shipley will return to a depth role in the backfield for the Eagles.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Activated From Injured Reserve
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley (foot, illness) was activated from injured reserve Saturday, the team announced. Philadelphia listed him as questionable for Sunday's Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers after he was limited Wednesday and Thursday and missed Friday's practice with an illness. Shipley last played in Week 5, when he started against the Jacksonville Jaguars with Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby sidelined. He scored on a two-yard run before leaving with the foot injury that cost him four games. Barkley practiced in full all week and carries no injury designation. He took 13 of the 16 carries by Eagles running backs against the New York Giants before the bye. Practice squad call-up Elijah Mitchell handled the other three and caught three passes. Jaydon Blue rejoined the active roster Tuesday and has one catch and zero carries this season. Blue returned six kickoffs against the Giants, a role Shipley held before getting hurt. With Bigsby still on injured reserve, Shipley is a potential handcuff for Barkley managers in deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Will Shipley (foot/illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
metadata.analysis: The team recently opened the 21-day practice window for Shipley, and he may be back in the lineup on Sunday, as he is currently considered questionable to play. His path to play is now more complicated thanks to an illness that he picked up, and fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to have a big role even if he's fully cleared to make his return this week.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Questionable, still on IR
metadata.description: Shipley (foot/illness) didn't practice Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest versus the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Since the Eagles designated Shipley to return from injured reserve Monday, he managed back-to-back limited practices to begin Week 11 prep before Friday's absence, which seemingly can be attributed to an illness. The team will need to activate Shipley from IR by Saturday afternoon for him to have a chance to play Sunday. If he gets the all clear, Shipley will be joining a backfield that's still led by Saquon Barkley, with Jaydon Blue and potentially practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell also available.

metadata.title: Will Shipley is Tagged as Questionable for Week 11
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley (foot, illness) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's Week 11 contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Shipley was recently designated to return from the Injured Reserve. He managed to get through back-to-back limited practice sessions before sitting out on Friday due to an illness. His path to playing is now more complicated due to the illness he picked up late in the week. Even if he's active, Shipley isn't expected to have a major role in the Eagles' backfield this weekend. He figures to be mixed in as a change-of-pace back to Saquon Barkley. He'll likely only offer deep league value, assuming he's active this weekend.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Could Immediately Resume No. 2 Duties if Available
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley (foot/illness) is nearing a return, and could be back in the lineup for a Week 11 contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Shipley has been on injured reserve since Oct. 16 after partially tearing his plantar fascia against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5. While the Eagles will still need to activate Shipley off of IR for him to play against the Steelers, the team designated him for return by opening his 21-day practice window on Monday. Shipley logged two consecutive limited practice sessions to start the week, but he did not practice on Friday. He enters Sunday's game against Pittsburgh with a questionable designation. The Eagles will have starter Saquon Barkley available this week against the Steelers, and other running back options include Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell (practice squad). If Shipley is able to play, though, he should return to a No. 2 role behind Barkley in Philadelphia's depleted running back room. It has been an inefficient and injury-riddled season for Shipley. Through five appearances, Shipley has recorded 20 carries for 57 yards (2.9 yards per carry) and a touchdown, while adding five catches (on eight targets) for 31 receiving yards (6.2 yards per reception). Barkley, who has dealt with various injuries of his own in 2026, will lead the backfield, and so long as he is healthy enough, he should dominate touches versus Pittsburgh. If Shipley is active, there are certainly opportunities for a few touches of his own. With that in mind, coming off of a foot injury and with Barkley ahead of him, there is no reason to add Shipley right now. He is currently owned in just 2% of Yahoo leagues and will have to prove himself to see that number increase.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Shipley (foot) remained limited in practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Shipley is still on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened this week. With Saquon Barkley healthy right now, Shipley has minimal fantasy appeal in a broken Philadelphia offense that is near the bottom of the league in most categories over the last month.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Officially limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Shipley (foot) was a limited practice participant Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Shipley sustained a partial tear of his plantar fascia in Week 5 against the Jaguars in London, resulting in an IR stint. He missed the last four games before a Week 10 bye before the Eagles designated him for return Monday. No. 1 RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) practiced fully Wednesday, so if Shipley gains clearance to play Sunday versus the Steelers, it'll likely be in a complementary role out of the backfield.

metadata.title: Will Shipley has practice window opened
metadata.description: The Eagles opened the practice window of RB Will Shipley.
metadata.analysis: Shipley will have 21 days to be officially activated.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Practice window being opened
metadata.description: The Eagles opened Shipley's (foot) 21-day practice window Monday.
metadata.analysis: Shipley landed on IR after being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the wake of Week 5 action, but he now has a chance to play as soon as Sunday against the Steelers. Meanwhile, fellow RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) -- who hasn't played since Week 4 -- remains on IR, and the Eagles signed Jaydon Blue to their practice squad Monday. If Shipley is able to suit up this weekend, he'll reclaim a backup role behind Saquon Barkley that isn't likely to result in much volume for the 2024 fourth-rounder.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Designated to Return From Injured Reserve
metadata.description: The Philadelphia Eagles designated running back Will Shipley (foot) to return from Injured Reserve by opening his 21-day practice window on Monday, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Sports. Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the team's Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and has been on IR ever since, but if he looks good in practice this week, he could have a chance to be officially activated and play this Sunday in Week 11 against the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers. Tank Bigsby (abdomen) also remains on IR, but if Shipley is activated before Bigsby, he would be in line to serve as the direct backup to starter Saquon Barkley, potentially making him a desperation flex option in the deepest of PPR fantasy football leagues. The 24-year-old Shipley, a fourth-rounder in 2024 from Clemson, had 20 rushing attempts for only 57 yards (2.9 yards per carry) and one touchdown in the first five games of the year, adding five catches on his eight targets for 31 yards in the passing game. Right now, Barkley is the only RB the Eagles have on their active roster, with Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue on the practice squad. Mitchell had a season-high 11 carries for 34 yards on Nov. 1 against the division-rival Washington Commanders with Barkley battling hamstring and back issues, but he had just three carries for six yards and three catches for 20 yards in the Week 9 loss to the division-rival New York Giants.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot) placed on IR
metadata.description: The Eagles placed RB Will Shipley on injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: Shipley will miss at least the next four weeks for the Eagles.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Placed on injured reserve
metadata.description: The Eagles placed Shipley (foot) on injured reserve Friday.
metadata.analysis: After being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia earlier this week, Shipley was slated for a multi-week absence, and he now will miss at least the next four games while on IR. He'll join Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on the list, and with Saquon Barkley currently tending to a lingering hamstring injury, the Eagles have just two healthy RBs (Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele) on the active roster. Shipley's next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 22 against the Steelers.

metadata.title: Eagles Place Will Shipley on Injured Reserve on Friday
metadata.description: The Philadelphia Eagles placed running back Will Shipley (foot) on Injured Reserve on Friday, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN. Shipley was a high-priority pickup off the waiver wire last week after Saquon Barkley injured his hamstring in the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, but he suffered a foot injury while in a starting role in last Sunday's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London and will now be forced to miss at least the next four games. The 24-year-old will join Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on IR, and with Barkley ruled out for a second straight game this weekend against the visiting Carolina Panthers, the Eagles will be down to Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele in their backfield in Week 6. Specifically, Shipley was diagnosed with a plantar-fascia tear in his foot, so fantasy managers should not be surprised if he misses more than the next four games. In many leagues where he was scooped off the waiver wire, Shipley can be cut. In his first five games of 2026, he has 20 rushing attempts for 57 yards and one touchdown while catching five passes for 31 yards. Shipley was the RB3 in Philly when both Barkley and Bigsby were healthy.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot) doesn't practice Thursday
metadata.description: Will Shipley (foot) officially did not practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, Shipley was a non-participant at practice on Thursday after recently suffering a major foot injury. He will almost certainly be sidelined in Week 6, leaving Dameon Pierce as the team's top back ahead of a matchup against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - DNP on Thursday
metadata.description: Shipley (foot) didn't practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Considering Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during this past Sunday's defeat to the Jaguars in London and is facing a multi-week absence, his lack of practice reps so far this week is expected. With No. 1 RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also not practicing Wednesday or Thursday, the Eagles may be preparing to deploy the duo of Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele out of their backfield Sunday against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Shipley (foot) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: It's not much of a surprise to see a DNP next to Shipley's name on the Eagles' first injury report of Week 6 prep, given that the third-year running back was diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia following the team's 19-17 Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. Shipley is facing a multi-week absence, and with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also idle for Wednesday's session, the Eagles may have to turn to Dameon Pierce to lead the backfield against the Panthers on Sunday.

metadata.title: Will Shipley suffers partial tear of plantar fascia
metadata.description: Eagles RB Will Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during Sunday's loss to the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Shipley is likely to miss multiple weeks. With Tank Bigsby on IR and Saquon Barkley still week-to-week, it could be Dameon Pierce leading the backfield in Week 6 against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Could face multi-week absence
metadata.description: Shipley (foot) was diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia after exiting Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London and could be sidelined multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Called upon to make his second career start with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) out for Week 5 and with Tank Bigsby (core) on injured reserve, Shipley played just 13 snaps and accounted for 13 yards and a touchdown on six touches (five carries, one reception) before leaving the game in the second quarter. After his foot injury was revealed to be a plantar fascia tear, Shipley now appears likely to be sidelined for at least next Sunday's game versus Carolina. Barkley is being viewed as week-to-week, and if both he and Shipley end up missing more time, the Eagles could be left with Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as well as practice-squad member Jaydon Blue as their backfield options for Week 6.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Could Miss Multiple Weeks With Plantar Fascia Tear
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley (foot) suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and could miss multiple weeks, according to NFL insider Adam Schefter. Making his first start of 2026 with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) sidelined and Tank Bigsby (core muscle) on injured reserve, Shipley gained six yards and scored a two-yard touchdown on five carries before leaving in the second quarter. He also caught one of two targets for seven yards. The injury adds another complication to Philadelphia's backfield ahead of its Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers. Dameon Pierce handled most of the rushing work following Shipley's departure, finishing with just 14 yards on 11 carries, while Carson Steele did not record an offensive touch. Pierce could see another substantial workload if Barkley remains sidelined, although the Eagles managed only 22 rushing yards against Jacksonville. Shipley's potential multiweek absence leaves his short-term fantasy value in doubt, while Pierce's relevance will depend largely on Barkley's recovery and whether Philadelphia adds further backfield depth.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot) ruled out Sunday
metadata.description: Will Shipley (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars according to Jeff McLane.
metadata.analysis: Shipley exited with the foot injury in the first half, rushing five times for six yards and one touchdown before suffering the injury. Dameon Pierce will handle the bulk of the backfield work for head coach Nick Sirianni for the remainder of the game.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Won't return to Sunday's game
metadata.description: The Eagles ruled out Shipley (foot) for the remainder of Sunday's game versus the Jaguars in London.
metadata.analysis: With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) ruled out for Week 5 and Tank Bigsby (core) landing on injured reserve, Shipley looked poised to handle a featured role out of the Philadelphia backfield. However, Shipley's day came to an end late in the second quarter, when he sustained a foot injury that will ultimately keep him from returning. The Eagles will finish out the contest with Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as their main options out of the backfield. Shipley finished with five carries for six yards and a touchdown to go with a seven-yard reception on two targets.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot) questionable to return
metadata.description: Eagles RB Will Shipley is questionable to return against the Jaguars with a foot injury.
metadata.analysis: Shipley was injured on his last carry and went to the locker room for further evaluation. Dameon Pierce will handle the bulk of the carries with Shipley questionable to return.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Questionable to return Sunday
metadata.description: Shipley is questionable to return to Sunday's game versus the Jaguars in London due to a foot injury.
metadata.analysis: Shipley was dinged up after a carry in the second quarter and visited the medical tent on the Eagles sideline before going to the locker room. He was getting most of the backfield reps in place of an absent Saquon Barkley (hamstring) before his departure, and if Shipley is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest, the Eagles backfield likely will be paced by Dameon Pierce. Carson Steele is also on hand for reps.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Ruled Out With Foot Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Shipley suffered the injury during the second quarter and was evaluated in the medical tent before heading to the locker room. He had five carries for six yards and a touchdown, along with one reception for seven yards, before exiting. Shipley was handling the starting role with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) sidelined and Tank Bigsby (core) on injured reserve. Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are now Philadelphia's remaining options in the backfield.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Questionable to Return in Week 5 with Foot Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley (foot) exited during the first half of Sunday's Week 5 contest against the Jacksonville Jaguars and is officially questionable to return, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic. Shipley left midway through the second quarter, but not before scoring the first touchdown of his young career. At the time of his departure, he had five carries, six rushing yards, one catch, seven receiving yards, and the score. Shipley earned the start this week and had been handling a substantially larger workload with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) inactive and Tank Bigsby (core) landing on injured reserve. Injury issues were already plaguing Philadelphia on both sides of the ball, and Shipley's foot ailment certainly won't help. Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are now the Eagles' only healthy running backs, and neither of them was even on the active roster at this time last week.

metadata.title: Will Shipley to Start Sunday, Will Handle the Bulk of the Workload
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley is expected to earn the start on Sunday, according to Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia. The third-year back will occupy an expanded role with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (core) both sidelined for Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Not only is Shipley earning the start, but he is also in line to handle the bulk of the workload, leaving fewer opportunities for players like Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. While fantasy managers remain disappointed that Barkley and Bigsby are unavailable, Shipley should still emerge as a high-end RB3 or low-end RB2. After all, he looked solid in the aftermath of injuries to Barkley and Bigsby last Sunday, rushing for 23 yards on six carries while handling a 48% snap share. The game script for Sunday against Jacksonville isn't great, but we still expect Shipley to carve out a sizable role.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Philly's top RB for Week 5
metadata.description: Shipley will lead the Eagles' backfield against the Jaguars on Week 5 due to the absences of both Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen, IR), Chris McPherson of the Eagles' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley and Bigsby both sustained injuries during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams, and with both running backs sidelined for Week 5, the Eagles will turn to Shipley to handle RB1 duties while Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele provide backfield depth. Shipley is averaging 3.4 yards per carry though four games this season, and his work will be cut out for him against a Jaguars defense that allows the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL (74.3).

metadata.title: Will Shipley Poised for Increased Role in Week 5
metadata.description: There is a big opportunity available for Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley in a Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. Shipley, who normally operates as the third-string running back for the Eagles, could be thrust into a starting role on Sunday due to injuries to starter Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and backup tailback Tank Bigsby (abdomen). Both Barkley and Bigsby were injured during the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4. Barkley was injured on the second series of the game after just four offensive snaps, while Bigsby and Shipley each played 29 snaps against the Rams. However, it was Bigsby leading the way before he exited the game late with the core injury. Bigsby recorded 14 carries for 55 yards (3.9 yards per carry), while Shipley tallied six rushes for 23 yards (3.8 yards per carry). With Barkley ruled out and Bigsby now on injured reserve, Shipley appears to be in a position to lead Philadelphia's backfield in Week 5. However, the Eagles did sign both Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele off of their practice squad and added them to the 53-man roster ahead of Week 5. Pierce is likely to be involved as well. So far in 2026, Shipley has played 91 offensive snaps and 63 snaps on special teams. He has recorded 15 rushes for 51 yards (3.4 yards per carry) and four receptions for 24 yards (6.0 yards per catch). Shipley has not yet scored a touchdown during the regular season in his career, but he did do so in the playoffs during the 2024 season. Shipley should have an opportunity for increased touches, but he faces a tough matchup against a Jacksonville defense that ranks third in the NFL with 74.3 rushing yards per game allowed. According to Pro Football Reference, the Jaguars rank third in the NFL in fantasy points given up per game to running backs (11.1). Shipley currently ranks as RotoBaller's No. 32 running back for Week 5. After being off of the fantasy radar, Shipley saw a 47% increase in his rostered percentage in Yahoo leagues from Week 4 to Week 5, but he is still available in 52% of leagues.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Could See Lead Role in Eagles Backfield in Week 5
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley has seen most of his usage on special teams since entering the NFL in 2024, recording just 76 total touches across 35 career games with the Eagles. However, the 24-year-old could get his chance to lead the Philadelphia backfield in the team's upcoming Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is considered unlikely to play against Jacksonville with a hamstring injury, and RB2 Tank Bigsby (core) is set to undergo core muscle surgery and will be placed on Injured Reserve. As a result, Shipley could be called upon to play a three-down role against the Jaguars. In leagues where he remains available on the waiver wire, Shipley profiles as a must-add running back for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Emerging as a Waiver-Wire Target Amid Eagles' Backfield Injuries
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley has played a minimal role in his team's offense so far in 2026, recording 75 yards from scrimmage on 19 touches across four games. However, injuries could be opening the door for Shipley to see more opportunities going forward. Eagles RB1 Saquon Barkley (hamstring) left the team's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams with a hamstring injury and could now be looking at additional missed time. Additionally, Eagles RB2 Tank Bigsby (groin) left the game late in the fourth quarter and may now be battling a groin injury. Neither Barkley nor Bigsby is guaranteed to miss time, which is likely what it would take for Shipley to emerge as a must-start fantasy running back. Still, Shipley offers a three-down skill set, and he could have a chance to play a lead role in the Philadelphia backfield. In most fantasy leagues, Shipley is worth targeting on the waiver wire just in case Barkley and Bigsby are unable to play in Week 5.  Update - According to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network, Bigsby is set to undergo core muscle surgery and will be placed on the injured reserve. As a result, Shipley could lead the backfield in Week 5 if Barkley remains sidelined, making him a top waiver wire target.

metadata.title: Will Shipley quiet in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Will Shipley rushed the ball six times for 23 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: Shipley saw six touches on Sunday, but he was only able to turn them into 23 yards against the Rams, which left him with a poor fantasy total. He may see more work than usual moving forward if starter Saquon Barkley has to miss time with his hamstring injury.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Team's other two RBs hurt Week 4
metadata.description: Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams. He also returned three kickoffs for 65 yards.
metadata.analysis: Shipley was the last man standing in Philadelphia's backfield after Saquon Barkley (hamstring) exited in the first quarter and Tank Bigsby (undisclosed) left in the fourth quarter. Bigsby had been working ahead of Shipley after Barkley's exit, but if neither of Philadelphia's top two running backs are available in Week 5, Shipley could take on the lead role against the Jaguars in London.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Avoids injury designation for Week 4
metadata.description: Shipley (foot) practiced in full on Friday and does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Rams.
metadata.analysis: Shipley has been battling a foot injury. He didn't practice Wednesday and was limited Thursday. However, after logging a full session Friday, the 24-year-old is good to go for the Week 4 meeting with Los Angeles. Shipley is second on the team in snaps at the running back position behind Saquon Barkley, though he hasn't done much, amassing 28 yards off nine carries throughout the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign.

metadata.title: Will Shipley (foot) cleared to play Sunday

metadata.analysis: The running back is apparently dealing with a foot injury as the practice week begins for Philadelphia. Shipley carried the ball seven times for 24 yards and caught two passes for five yards in the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans last Sunday, seeing an expanded role with Saquon Barkley on the bench for much of the game. Barkley (shoulder) was limited Thursday, and Shipley could play a bigger role again if the starter can't go this coming Monday at Chicago, but that will depend on the Clemson product's status.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Elevated role after Barkley injury
metadata.description: Shipley turned seven carries into 24 yards and caught both of his targets for five yards during the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Both Shipley and Tank Bigsby operated in larger roles in the Eagles' backfield after Saquon Barkley left in the first quarter due to a shoulder stinger. During that time that Barkley was off the field, Shipley operated as the clear RB2 behind Bigsby, with Shipley's seven carries being his most in a game since the 2024 season, when he logged eight carries or more three times. Barkley's practice participation over the coming days will be worth monitoring, as Shipley would be primed to serve as Philadelphia's RB2 against Chicago on Monday if Barkley is not cleared to play.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Could be a Deep-League Stash Option
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley saw more involvement than expected during the Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans. Normally, Shipley only gets a carry or two, but he played over 50 percent of the offensive snaps on Sunday. His increased playing time was because Saquon Barkley (stinger) was forced to exit the game in the first half. Shipley did a nice job filling in as he carried the ball seven times for 24 yards, while hauling in both targets for five additional yards. At the moment, it's unclear if Barkley will be ready to go for the Monday Night matchup against the Chicago Bears. Given the fact that Barkley is banged up, Shipley is worth a look as a deep league stash with the possibility of an increased workload in Week 3.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Falls off the Fantasy Radar
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley was barely seen on the field during the Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders. Shipley rushed the ball twice for four yards while hauling in his lone target for eight yards in the victory. Shipley saw minimal work in the backfield behind workhorse back Saquon Barkley. The expectation is that the Eagles will continue to mix in Tank Bigsby and Shipley sparingly when Barkley needs a break. It's unlikely that either back offers a ton of weekly value while Barkley is healthy. Between the two backs, Bigsby is the much better handcuff for fantasy managers. Shipley belongs on the waiver wire in most formats until he proves otherwise.

metadata.title: Will Shipley sees three touches in Week 1
metadata.description: Will Shipley rushed twice for four yards while also catching his only target for eight yards in the Eagles' 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Shipley saw minimal involvement out of the backfield, with No. 1 running back Saquon Barkley out-touching him 16-3 in the win. The running back can remain off rosters until further notice, with a Week 2 contest against the Tennessee Titans up next.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Gets on stat sheet
metadata.description: Shipley recorded two carries for four yards, one catch for eight yards, one kickoff return for 25 yards and one tackle on punt coverage in Sunday's 24-22 win over the Commanders.
metadata.analysis: The running back actually got more carries than fellow backup Tank Bigsby, but Saquon Barkley saw the vast majority out of Philadelphia's backfield. Shipley can contribute in multiple ways, but he is not a fantasy-relevant running back at this point.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Is Firmly Third in Philadelphia's Backfield
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley played well enough this summer, but nothing he did changed his place in the backfield. Shipley rushed for 56 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries against New England and comfortably survived final cuts. He also enters Week 1 behind both Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby. Bigsby separated himself as the primary backup during camp after rushing for 344 yards and two touchdowns on only 58 carries last season, while Shipley barely touched the ball on offense. He finished 2025 with 14 carries for 49 yards and nine catches for 56 yards, doing much more of his work on special teams. Philadelphia kept only three running backs on the initial 53-man roster, so Shipley's standing is pretty clear. There is some contingency value if injuries start piling up, and his receiving ability gives the Eagles another option. For fantasy purposes, though, Bigsby is the insurance back behind Barkley. Shipley is difficult to justify in ordinary redraft leagues while he remains third in line.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Slipping Off the Redraft Radar
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley has a tough path to fantasy relevance entering his third season. He barely touched the ball in 2025, finishing with 14 carries for 49 yards and nine catches for 56 yards, while most of his work came as a kick returner. That part of his job is still safe. Philadelphia lists Shipley first at kick returner, but the offensive depth chart is another story. Saquon Barkley is first, Tank Bigsby is second, and Shipley is in the third group. Bigsby averaged 5.9 yards per carry after joining the Eagles last season, and he has continued getting meaningful work in camp. During Tuesday's run-out-the-clock period, Barkley and Bigsby were the backs getting carries. Barkley did have his left foot and ankle checked by a trainer Thursday, but there is no diagnosis yet and nothing to suggest Shipley suddenly moves up. His receiving ability gives Philadelphia another option if injuries pile up, but right now he looks more useful to the Eagles than to fantasy managers. In standard redraft leagues, Shipley is hard to justify as anything more than a very deep stash.

metadata.title: Will Shipley Trending Toward an Emergency Role
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley has displayed excellent efficiency in the passing game through his first two seasons in the league, catching nearly 93% of his targets on a very small sample size, but his current spot on the depth chart suggests little opportunity to expand his role in 2026. Through the early days of training camp, Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby have been splitting work close to evenly, and The Athletic's Brooks Kubena does not believe another back on the roster will see more than 30 touches this season. Kubena includes Shipley as the third running back on his initial 53-man roster projection, primarily for his role on special teams and points out that his pass-catching ability could become useful in an emergency. Barkley has touched the ball more than 800 times across his first two seasons with the Eagles, and Bigsby has been an early camp standout, tabbed for a larger role in his first full season with the team, leaving little opportunity for Shipley, who is unlikely to factor into fantasy plans for 2026.

metadata.title: Will Shipley an NFL Depth Piece with Little Fantasy Value
metadata.description: With training camps set to open at the end of the month, depth charts around the league will soon be tested, but one of the deepest rosters in the NFL still belongs to the Philadelphia Eagles, and at the running back spot in particular, third-year veteran Will Shipley provides a luxury to a team with title aspirations. Three-time Pro Bowler Saquon Barkley is firmly entrenched atop the depth chart, but with the 29-year-old back having accumulated more than 800 total touches across his first two seasons with the Eagles, the presence of Shipley and 2025 trade acquisition Tank Bigsby could allow him to keep fresh during the dog days of summer while each competes to carve out their own role. Through his own two seasons in Philadelphia, Shipley has carried the ball only 44 times for an unimpressive 131 yards, but his contributions on special teams boost his chances of sticking on the roster. While he carries little standalone fantasy value into 2026, Shipley would become a popular waiver add should an unfortunate injury strain the Eagles' impressive depth.

metadata.title: Will Shipley - Step back in second season
metadata.description: Shipley finished his second professional season with 14 carries for 49 yards and added nine receptions for 56 yards in 15 regular-season games.
metadata.analysis: While Shipley played nearly twice as many offensive snaps as he did as a rookie, his total touches dropped from 34 to 23. The 2024 fifth-round pick doesn't appear to be viewed as anything other than a depth option by the Eagles, as the team acquired Tank Bigsby from the Jaguars after Week 2 to serve as Saquon Barkley's primary backup.
